thread:
maya (PM): Quick design question — for the autoscale panel, should the Burst toggle be exposed on the main card or nested under 'Advanced'?
samir (prod-designer): leaning main card. Burst is a common ask and we want it discoverable. but we need to avoid accidental toggles. :warning:
tal (frontend): Agree discoverable, but we should change the control to a two-step: toggle + confirm slider. so toggle alone won't change cost. small pattern: toggle -> expand with slider + confirmation CTA.
liam (eng-run): Two-step is fine, but keep keyboard focus order sane. expanding panel must trap focus to the slider and confirm/cancel. after cancel, focus returns to the toggle.
nana (a11y): tiny nit: use aria-expanded on the toggle and add descriptive aria-live region for the confirmation status. also confirm/cancel must be real buttons, not links.
samir (prod-designer): Copy idea for the confirmation: "Enable burst capacity for short traffic spikes — estimated additional cost: ~${estimated}/hr" with an inline link to docs. Thoughts?
liam (eng-run): we can compute a ballpark estimate client-side if we add a usage-profile sample. but don't promise exact numbers. maybe say "approx."
maya (PM): Good call. Also UX question: min/max fields — should we let users type in GPU counts or restrict to + / - stepper?
tal (frontend): For touch/precision, both. stepper + direct input. but validate on blur and show guardrail tooltip if they pick > pool size.
samir (prod-designer): And how do we indicate incompatible pool selection? e.g., selecting an 8-GPU model but pool only has 4-GPU nodes. Error inline? disable choices?
liam (eng-run): I prefer greying out incompatible pools with an info hover explaining why. If they force it (advanced override), show a warning modal explaining fallback routing to smaller model variant or queued requests.
nana (a11y): Ensure the disabled option still exposes the reason in accessible text — screen readers don't get hover. Put the reason in the option's aria-label.
maya (PM): SLO slider: product wants an easy "latency vs cost" knob. current mock shows a 0-100 slider. Is that too abstract?
samir (prod-designer): we tried 0-100 to avoid committing to ms. but teams keep asking "what does 70 mean". proposal: keep slider but add three presets: Low latency (SLO 95ms), Balanced (SLO 200ms), Cost saver (SLO 500ms). Show the SLO numbers in a tooltip.
tal (frontend): Presets are neat. Need to ensure keyboard users can pick presets and the slider updates aria-valuetext to "SLO target: 200ms".
liam (eng-run): Backend needs to accept both a numeric SLO and a preset enum. Schema: { "slo_ms": 200 } or { "slo_preset": "balanced" } — simple.
maya (PM): Guardrails: when user picks < 50ms on a pool that can't meet it, we should warn and suggest dedicated capacity. modal or inline warning?
samir (prod-designer): Inline banner is less interruptive: "This pool may not achieve the selected SLO. Consider Dedicated or a higher-tier pool." with quick actions: "Request Dedicated" / "Continue anyway".
liam (eng-run): "Continue anyway" should attach a flag that enables automatic fallback routing to hosted models if queues grow past X. backend needs that flag.
nana (a11y): Banner must be perceivable: use role="alert" so screen readers announce it. Color contrast must hit AA. Avoid only color cues for severity.
samir (prod-designer): Copy tweak for min/max labels: change "Min"/"Max" to "Min instances" / "Max instances" — less ambiguous.
tal (frontend): Agree. Also show a small info icon with hover: "Total GPUs = instances × GPUs per node".
maya (PM): Edge case: if user sets min=0 and burst is enabled, do we allow ephemeral instances to spin up? how to reflect that in the UI?
liam (eng-run): Yes, ephemeral burst instances can go below min when min=0. Need a line in the UI: "Ephemeral burst instances may be created temporarily" with a tooltip on behavior and billing.
samir (prod-designer): Maybe a small gray subline under the min control: "Min 0 allows zero baseline; burst may add temporary instances — billed while running."
nana (a11y): Make sure that subline is in the DOM order near the control and not only in a tooltip. Tooltips are not reliable for screen readers.
maya (PM): One more: GPU pool dropdown ordering — should we sort by latency (best), cost (cheapest), or user last-used?
samir (prod-designer): Suggest: default sort = recommended (latency + cost score), allow user to switch to "most used" or "cheapest" via a small toggle in the dropdown header.
tal (frontend): Implementing header controls inside native select is messy. We should use a custom combobox with proper ARIA roles.
liam (eng-run): Backend can provide pool metadata: {"latency_score": 0.8, "cost_score": 0.3, "id": "pool-a"}. Frontend comp sorts.
maya (PM): deploy-bot will post a deploy preview of the new panel later today — please test keyboard first.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: preview/redwood-internal/autoscale-ui-v3 -> staging. Build #8342.
tal (frontend): I'll test keyboard flow + screen reader on the preview and post issues here.
samir (prod-designer): I'll update the mock to show the banner and presets and push assets to Figma.
maya (PM): Thanks team — capture any copy nits in the Figma comments and tag me. Done for now. :rocket:
